• Original styling & rare find: Unlike mass-market toys, each detail is thoughtfully designed from scratch.

📖 Page-by-Page FAIRY GARDEN (see more in photos of each book for details):
1. Mushroom house in the flower garden (cover page) - Let's flip the soft felt leaves to peek inside your fairy’s cozy home.

5. The worm eating through the pear - Using the string to guide the worm through holes - strengthen fine motor skills and focus

From page 8 - for full version only

9. Unicorn ribbon mane - Weave and unweave the silky ribbons, then fan out the mane for magical flair.
10. Silly worm & carrot zipper play - Zip open to reveal the stretchy worm—pop out, stretch, and hide again!
11. Peek-a-Boo Bunny - Flip the bunny’s hands over its eyes to play classic “peek-a-boo.”

📖 Page by Page: WILD LION (see more in photos of each book for details):
1. Peek-a-boo lion (cover page) - Twist the lion’s arms in circles to cover—and uncover—his eyes in classic peek a boo fun.
2. Zebra leaf tug - Let your baby sway the zebra’s two legs, then pull the soft leaves side to side to reveal hidden stripes.
3. Banana-eating monkey - Zip and unzip the pouch; guide the banana into the monkey’s mouth. Spin the button eye through its safe mesh track, then lift the leaf flap for extra surprise.
4. Bear brushing teeth - Tiny toothbrush in paw—builds dexterity and reinforces healthy habits.
5. Birthday cake stacking - Hooks and loops cake layers stack from largest to smallest—early math and sequencing made sweet.
6. Sun ribbon rays & mirror - Thread the ribbons through loops to fan out sunbeams, then catch a smile of him/herself in the soft, safe and elastic mirror.
7. Elephant swing - Wiggle the elephant’s trunk side to side and feel the crinkle of its textured ears—sensory delight!
From page 8 - for full version only
8. Balloon riding bear - A tactile hand puppet bear in a fuzzy basket -- peel and stick the scratch and feel textures for extra grip.
9. Rainbow & rising sun - Pull the tab to raise or lower the sun behind a rainbow -- gentle cause and effect play.
10. Chestnut-eating worm - Guide the worm through holes in the chestnut shell -- threading practice for little fingers.
11. Airplane glide - Slide the plane diagonally across the page -- perfect for practicing smooth, guided motion.

📖 Page by Page: BERRY TALE (see more in photos of each book for details):
1. Berry sweet welcome (cover page) - Decorated with strawberries and a bow – sets the tone for a whimsical adventure.
2. Flower mirror - A soft cotton flower with a flexible, baby-safe mirror as its center. Great for self-recognition and finger exploration.
3. Peek-a-boo bunny with flower crown - The bunny’s hands flip open for peek-a-boo fun. The flower on the crown gently spins.
4. Cute pink owl on a branch - Mesh eyes with movable buttons inside – little fingers can slide them safely to explore movement.
5. Strawberry layer cupcake - Stack the soft hooks and loops cake layers from biggest to smallest. A cherry on top adds the perfect touch.
6. Mushroom house with fairy puppet - Open the buttoned door to reveal a surprise – a tiny fairy puppet waiting inside!
7. Unicorn ribbon mane - Weave and unweave the silky ribbons, then fan out the mane for magical flair.
From page 8 - for full version only
8. Giraffe brushing teeth - Open the giraffe’s mouth and help it brush its teeth – a great fine motor and help develop good habit & self-care skill.
9. Worm eating through the apple - Using the string to guide the worm through holes - strengthen fine motor skills and focus.
10. Silly worm & carrot zipper play - Zip open to reveal the stretchy worm—pop out, stretch, and hide again!
11. Snail hiding behind the leaf - Lift the big leaf flap to find a sliding snail hiding! Move it gently side-to-side along a soft track.

📖 Page by Page: BEAR ADVENTURE (see more in photos of each book for details):
1. Peek-a-boo bear in a party hat (cover page) - A cheerful brown bear wears a birthday hat and lifts both arms for a fun peek-a-boo greeting.
2. Birthday cake stacking - Stack soft hooks and loops cake layers from largest to smallest and top it with a felt flame — a sweet sorting game!
3. Sun rising from the rainbow - Pull the sun string up and down as it peeks out from behind the rainbow — early cause-and-effect play.
4. Bear riding balloon - A smiling bear in a hot air balloon — use as a finger puppet for interactive storytelling.
5. Flying plane fun - Slide the airplane up and down diagonally with fingertip control — simple motion with big excitement!
6. Elephant with flapping ears - Big, crinkly ears flap wide like fans. Move the trunk in circles, lift the legs, and swipe the big green leaves back and forth. Sensory delight!
7. Silly worm eating pear – zip play - A stretchy, silly worm hides inside a pear — zip open and shut to discover and hide it again.
From page 8 - for full version only
8. Sun ribbon rays & mirror - Thread the ribbons through loops to fan out sunbeams, then catch a smile of him/herself in the soft, safe and elastic mirror.
9. Owl on a branch - Mesh eyes with movable buttons inside – little fingers can slide them safely to explore movement.
10. Hippo brushing teeth - Lift the hippo’s big mouth and use the tiny toothbrush to help brush! Builds good habits and strengthens fine motor control.
11. Chestnut-eating worm - Guide the worm through holes in the chestnut shell -- threading practice for little fingers.
